```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/fdr_panel10nc"; BA <- "docs/assets/fdr_panel10"
ov <- fread(file.path(A, "fdr_overview.tsv")); vb <- fread(file.path(A, "overview_vs_base.tsv"))
rounds <- fread(file.path(A, "adaptive_rounds.tsv")); cons <- fread(file.path(A, "consistency.tsv"))
g <- fread(file.path(A, "significant_genes.tsv")); gb <- fread(file.path(BA, "significant_genes.tsv"))
gc <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_changes.tsv")); cs <- fread(file.path(A, "compare_summary.tsv"))
ga <- fread(file.path(A, "gained.tsv")); lo <- fread(file.path(A, "lost.tsv")); nts <- fread(file.path(A, "newly_tested_summary.tsv"))
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
pct <- function(x, digits=0) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), 100 * x)
counts <- function(a, b) sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt(a), fmt(b))
any_tp <- ov[tp == "any timepoint"]; any_vb <- vb[tp == "any timepoint"]
effect_reads <- function(d, t) fifelse(is.na(d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]]), "no score",
  sprintf("%+.0f (%s)", 100 * d[[paste0("dpsi_", t)]], fmt(d[[paste0("het_cov_", t)]])))
best_q <- function(d) signif(pmin(d$q_bh_0hr, d$q_bh_1hr, d$q_bh_6hr, na.rm=TRUE), 2)
example_table <- function(genes, why) {
  d <- g[match(genes, gene)]
  data.table(Gene=d$gene, `0 hr`=effect_reads(d, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(d, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(d, "6hr"),
             `Best q`=best_q(d), `Het donors`=d$max_het, Relevance=why)
}
pattern_labels <- c("all three timepoints"="Significant at 3 timepoints",
                    "two timepoints"="Significant at 2 timepoints",
                    "shared, below threshold elsewhere"="One timepoint; nominal support elsewhere",
                    "candidate timepoint-specific"="One timepoint; no nominal support elsewhere",
                    "not testable elsewhere"="One timepoint; no usable score elsewhere")
g[, display_pattern := unname(pattern_labels[pattern])]
annot <- function(d) d[, .(`Neuronal GO term`=neuronal_go,
  `Developmental disorder or autism`=fifelse(nzchar(sfari) & nzchar(ddg2p), paste0(sfari, "; ", ddg2p), paste0(sfari, ddg2p)),
  `Expression after stimulation`=expression_response, `Splicing after stimulation`=fifelse(stim_splicing, "yes", ""))]
interactive_table <- function(d) DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10, lengthMenu=c(10, 25, 50), scrollX=TRUE, order=list(), dom="Blfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")),
  caption="Search or filter genes, sort columns, and export the filtered table as CSV.")
new_genes <- gc[status == "this run only", gene]; both_genes <- gc[status == "both", gene]
n_gained <- nrow(ga); n_gained_genes <- uniqueN(ga$gene)
nb_type <- function(d) fifelse(d$n_neighbours == 0, "none", fifelse(d$n_neighbours_unsupported == 0, "panel variants only",
  fifelse(d$n_neighbours_in_panel == 0, "unsupported calls only", "both kinds")))
rc <- fread(file.path(A, "gained_read_check.tsv"))
read_status <- function(d) { x <- rc[match(paste(d$tp, d$Gene_name, d$variant_qual, d$exonic_part), paste(rc$tp, rc$Gene_name, rc$variant_qual, rc$exonic_part))]
  fifelse(x$reads_status == "reported", "reported", fifelse(x$reads_status == "not tested", "not testable",
          fifelse(is.na(x$dpsi_reads), "tested, no score", sprintf("ΔPSI %+.2f, not reported", x$dpsi_reads)))) }
```

**Transcript-based isoLASER** labels each read as including or excluding an
exonic part from the transcript isoLASER assigned it to, as isoLASER itself does.
We keep it to compare with our main analysis,
[read-based isoLASER](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html), which labels each read from its
own alignment. This page is the genome-wide permutation FDR without the
clustering filter; the [run with the filter](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html) remains as
an earlier setup.

**Setup (our definitions):**

- **No clustering filter.** It was added for the original run, where
  donors were chosen by their RNA allele fraction: a cluster of variant calls is
  often misaligned reads rather than real SNPs. Here every tested SNP must already
  be heterozygous in our genotype panel, so we dropped the filter; the comparison
  below shows what it had removed.
- **As in the filtered run:** isoLASER's inclusion labels (from each read's assigned transcript),
  panel-heterozygous donors with ≥ 10 reads, every recorded variant × exonic part,
  ≥ 20 reads over the donors used and a part of ≥ 10 bp in the tested family, the
  shuffles, isoLASER's scoring functions, the adaptive rounds, BH within each
  timepoint, and the `cis` / |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10 screen.
- **Checks:** before comparing, we confirmed for every chromosome × timepoint
  that both runs are finished and current. They use the same isoLASER
  recordings, the same association list and genotype inputs, and identical
  unshuffled scores in round 1, so the runs differ only in the clustering filter. As in
  every run, each unshuffled score was rebuilt independently, and all 66
  chromosome × timepoint checks matched.
- **Not yet done:** calibration runs.

**Main result:** `r fmt(any_tp$q05_associations)` associations in
**`r fmt(any_tp$q05_genes)` genes** have q < 0.05 and pass the screen,
against `r fmt(any_vb$base_q05_associations)` in `r fmt(any_vb$base_q05_genes)`
genes in the run with the clustering filter. No association reported there is lost here.
`r n_gained` association × timepoint results are gained, in `r n_gained_genes` genes;
`r length(new_genes)` of these genes are not reported in the run with the clustering filter at all
(`r paste(new_genes, collapse=", ")`). Most gained results belong to genes whose effects vanish with read-based
labels (below), so they reflect transcript assignment rather than allelic
splicing.

# Genome-wide results

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(ov[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Tested associations`=fmt(tested),
  `Paper's cutoff`=counts(paper_associations, paper_genes),
  Screen=counts(screen_associations, screen_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.10`=counts(q10_associations, q10_genes),
  `Screen + q < 0.05`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes))], align="lrrrrr")
```

Cells other than **Tested associations** show **associations (genes)**.
**Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` call with no other filter, as in the
isoLASER paper; it does not depend on our family rules, so it is the same as on
the page with the clustering filter. **Screen** (our definition), before FDR control: among the
tested associations, isoLASER's `cis` rule computed on the panel-heterozygous
donors only, plus |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10. **Any timepoint** counts each gene or
association once across timepoints. BH targets FDR within each timepoint's full
family; the effect-filtered subset and the union across timepoints have no
separate 5% FDR guarantee.

# Compared with the run with the clustering filter

```{r vs_base}
knitr::kable(merge(vb, cs[, .(tp, kept, gained, lost)], by="tp", all.x=TRUE)[match(c("0hr", "1hr", "6hr", "any timepoint"), tp),
  .(Timepoint=tp, `Tested: with filter`=fmt(base_tested), `Tested: this run`=fmt(tested),
    `Screen + q < 0.05: with filter`=counts(base_q05_associations, base_q05_genes),
    `Screen + q < 0.05: this run`=counts(q05_associations, q05_genes),
    Kept=fifelse(is.na(kept), "", fmt(kept)), Gained=fifelse(is.na(gained), "", fmt(gained)), Lost=fifelse(is.na(lost), "", fmt(lost)))],
  align="lrrrrrrr")
```

**Kept / Gained / Lost** count reported associations at each timepoint: reported
in both runs, only here, or only in the run with the clustering filter. Dropping the filter adds
`r pct(any_vb$tested / any_vb$base_tested - 1)` more tested associations; every
association tested in the run with the clustering filter is tested here too.

## Newly tested associations

These are the associations the clustering filter had removed. Each one's variant
has at least one other candidate variant within 30 bases, a **neighbour**:

```{r newly}
knitr::kable(nts[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Newly tested`=fmt(newly_tested), `Neighbours: panel variants only`=fmt(only_panel_neighbours),
  `Neighbours: unsupported calls only`=fmt(only_unsupported_neighbours), `Neighbours: both kinds`=fmt(both_kinds))], align="lrrrr")
```

A neighbour is a **panel variant** if our genotype panel has a single matching,
well-genotyped record (typed, or imputed with R² ≥ 0.8), whatever the donors'
genotypes. It is an **unsupported call** if the panel has no such record, or if it
is not a single-base variant. Most newly tested variants sit next to real panel
variants, that is, two real SNPs close together.

## Gained associations

```{r gained}
gd <- ga[order(tp, q_bh)]
knitr::kable(gd[, .(Timepoint=sub("hr", " hr", tp), Gene=gene, Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part, `Het donors`=n_het,
  `ΔPSI`=sprintf("%+.2f", dpsi), q=signif(q_bh, 2), `q with filter`=fifelse(is.na(q_bh_base), "not tested", as.character(signif(q_bh_base, 2))),
  Neighbours=nb_type(gd), MHC=fifelse(in_mhc, "yes", ""), `With read-based labels`=read_status(gd))])
```

**q with filter**: "not tested" for associations the clustering filter
removed; a value means the association was tested there and missed q < 0.05.
**Neighbours** describes the candidate variants within 30 bases, as above.
**MHC**: inside the major histocompatibility complex (chr6:28.5–33.5 Mb), the
most polymorphic region of the genome, where reads are often misaligned.
[Download the gained associations with each neighbour listed](assets/fdr_panel10nc/gained.tsv).

Most gained results add associations, through clustered variants, to genes
already reported in the run with the clustering filter: CST3, CYBA, PFKP and ZFAND2A, plus the new
ARF4. CST3's two variants lie inside the 13-base part tested on the the filtered run
page. `r ga[!is.na(q_bh_base), .N]` gained results were tested with the filter and
just missed q < 0.05 there (q = `r paste(range(signif(ga[!is.na(q_bh_base), q_bh_base], 2)), collapse="–")`); here they pass,
because BH's threshold rises when many small p-values join the family.

**With read-based labels** ([the same run without the clustering filter](isolaser_fdr_reads10nc.html)),
only `r rc[reads_status == "reported", .N]` of the `r n_gained` gained results are reported, both for
ENSG00000289047 in the MHC. Another `r rc[reads_status == "tested, not reported", .N]` are tested there and not reported; the
`r rc[reads_status == "tested, not reported" & !is.na(dpsi_reads), .N]` with a score have a median |ΔPSI| of
`r sprintf("%.3f", rc[reads_status == "tested, not reported" & !is.na(dpsi_reads), median(abs(dpsi_reads))])`, against `r sprintf("%.2f", rc[reads_status == "tested, not reported" & !is.na(dpsi_reads), median(abs(dpsi))])` here. The remaining `r rc[reads_status == "not tested", .N]` cannot be tested. In this run the
clustering filter was mostly removing transcript-assignment artefacts (our
reading).

**Genes.** Reported in both runs: `r length(both_genes)`. Only in the
run with the clustering filter: `r gc[status == "base only", .N]`. Only here:
`r paste(new_genes, collapse=", ")`.
[Download the gene comparison](assets/fdr_panel10nc/gene_changes.tsv).

# How the test works

The test is the one described on the [original page](isolaser_fdr.html#how-the-test-works),
with the donor rule and remaining family rules of the [run with the clustering filter](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html).

```{r rounds}
knitr::kable(rounds[, .(Timepoint=tp, `Stopped at 1,000`=fmt(stopped_1e3),
  `Stopped at 10,000`=fmt(stopped_1e4), `Stopped at 100,000`=fmt(stopped_1e5),
  `Reached 1,000,000`=fmt(reached_1e6))], align="lrrrr")
```

**Stopped** means at least 20 hits at that checkpoint, or no observed score
(p = 1). Every association with zero hits after a million shuffles has q < 0.05,
so more shuffles would not change the results.

![](assets/fdr_panel10nc/qq.png)

Real data only; there are no calibration runs for this run.

# Genes to follow up

```{r follow}
fu <- g[!grepl("0hr", sig_tps) & (neuronal | brain_disorder | stim_expression | stim_splicing)]
sashimi <- fread(file.path(A, "sashimi_summary.tsv"))
sashimi_table <- function(gn) {
  d <- sashimi[gene == gn][order(timepoint)]
  frac <- function(i, e) sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", i, i + e, 100 * i / (i + e))
  knitr::kable(d[, .(Timepoint=sub("hr", " hr", timepoint), Donors=donors,
    `REF inclusion (raw)`=frac(REF_i, REF_e), `ALT inclusion (raw)`=frac(ALT_i, ALT_e),
    `Test dPSI (normalized, pp)`=sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * normalized_dPSI))], align="llrrr")
}
qv <- function(gn, t) format(signif(g[gene == gn][[paste0("q_bh_", t)]], 2))
pv <- function(gn, t) format(signif(g[gene == gn][[paste0("p_", t)]], 1))
same <- merge(g[, .(gene, variant_qual, exonic_part)], gb[, .(gene, bv=variant_qual, bp=exonic_part)], by="gene")
FU <- c("KPNA2", "PARK7", "ZNF749", "ASAH1", "LMBRD1")
```

We apply the [same two conditions](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html#genes-to-follow-up)
as the page with the clustering filter: reported only after stimulation (at 1 or 6 hours, not at 0
hours), and neuron- or stimulation-related. `r nrow(fu)` genes meet both.
Five are shown, the same five as on the page with the clustering filter. Not shown, as there:
**ALDH3A2** (no 0-hour test) and **UBE2Q2P2** (a pseudogene). No new gene meets
both conditions. With read-based labels only PARK7 and ZNF749 remain; KPNA2,
ASAH1 and LMBRD1 are not supported by the reads
([read-based isoLASER](isolaser_fdr_reads10.html#compared-with-the-transcript-based-run)).

```{r highlight}
knitr::kable(example_table(c("KPNA2", "PARK7", "ZNF749", "ASAH1", "LMBRD1"), c("Synapse, synaptic signaling (GO)", "Neuron projection, neuron death (GO); the Parkinson's disease gene DJ-1",
  "Splicing after stimulation (our scan), at this exon's donor sites",
  "Farber disease; spinal muscular atrophy with progressive myoclonic epilepsy (DDG2P)",
  "Methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria, cblF type (DDG2P)")), align="lrrrrrl")
```

**0 / 1 / 6 hr**: allelic effect in percentage points, alternative minus
reference inclusion, with pooled informative coverage in brackets. **Best q**:
the lowest timepoint-specific q-value. **Het donors**: the largest number of
panel-heterozygous donors used, out of four.

For each of these genes the representative association, its donors and its reads
are the same as in the run with the clustering filter
(`r sum(same$gene %in% FU & same$variant_qual == same$bv & same$exonic_part == same$bp)` of
`r length(FU)` checked); only the q-values change slightly with the larger family.
The figures below are drawn from this run.

**How to read each gene's figures:**

- **Permutation test:** one panel per timepoint. Grey bars are the first 1,000
  shuffled scores; the blue line is the observed score (AMI). The p-value uses
  the full adaptive run, up to a million shuffles.
- **Read alignments:** isoLASER's `nigiri_plot` sashimi renderer with the
  project's plotting fixes. Reads are split into REF (blue) and ALT (orange) by
  isoLASER's allele assignments and pooled over the donors used at each
  timepoint (heterozygous in the panel, ≥ 10 reads). Yellow marks the tested
  part. Coverage and arc numbers are raw read counts, on one scale per gene.
  **Raw inclusion** comes from isoLASER's transcript assignment, so a read can
  count without reaching the plotted region. Each plot's subtitles give how many
  reads reach it. The test uses donor-normalized tables, so its dPSI can differ
  slightly from the raw counts.
- **Isoforms and haplotypes**, at 0 hours and at the significant timepoint,
  drawn like Fig. 2d of the isoLASER paper:
  - **Rows:** annotated transcripts with their GENCODE v44 name and Ensembl ID.
    **Novel** transcripts are IsoQuant models from our annotation, shown with
    their SQANTI3 category against GENCODE v44. NIC is a new combination of
    known splice sites; fusion spans two genes.
  - **Which rows:** the three transcripts with the most reads in each group are
    drawn, and a grey row sums the rest. Introns are shortened.
  - **Marks:** green is the tested part. Orange marks the tested SNP, plus the
    nearest in-phase SNP when that one is closer to the part.
  - **Numbers:** reads per transcript from each haplotype, labelled by the
    tested SNP's alleles, as raw counts summed over the donors used.
  - **PSI row:** each haplotype's inclusion from those raw counts: reads in
    transcripts that include the part, divided by all its reads, drawn and
    undrawn transcripts together.
  - **Test line:** ΔPSI and q are the test's values. The test pools
    donor-normalized tables, so its ΔPSI can differ slightly from the
    difference between the two raw PSIs.

## KPNA2

The tested part is a whole 100-base intron between exons 6 and 7. KPNA2-221
keeps it, and the other annotated transcripts splice it out. isoLASER counts
ALT (C) reads as keeping the intron more often than REF (T) reads: at 6 hours,
12.7% vs 2.5% (+12 pp, q = `r qv("KPNA2", "6hr")`). At 0 and 1 hours the difference is +8 and
+2 pp, below threshold. The tested SNP (rs12752) is in the first exon, 7.2 kb
upstream. In the three donors, all 20 heterozygous panel SNPs within the gene
are phased the same way, so T and C reads come from two whole-gene haplotypes. The
nearest SNP to the intron, rs4638, is 135 bases downstream, with G on the T
haplotype.

## PARK7

The first exon ends at one of two donor sites 58 bases apart, an alternative 5′
splice site, and both sites splice to the same next exon. The tested 12-base
part is the extra stretch of the longer first exon; the adjacent 46-base part
gives the same result. ALT (C) reads use the shorter exon more often than REF
(T) reads. The difference has the same direction at all three timepoints and in
both donors, and is largest at 1 hour (−17 pp, q = `r qv("PARK7", "1hr")`), the only
significant timepoint; at 0 and 6 hours it is −7 and −8 pp. This describes each
timepoint separately and is not a test of a change over time. The variant
(rs226249) lies in the first exon, 18 bases before the shorter exon's donor
site.

## ZNF749

The tested part is a 355-base alternative last exon. Transcripts that use it
end there, and the others continue to exons further downstream. REF (G) reads
end in it far more often than ALT (C) reads. The difference is significant only
at 6 hours (−74 pp, q = `r qv("ZNF749", "6hr")`); at 0 and 1 hours it is −26 and −17 pp and below
threshold. In our stimulation splicing scan, the balance between the two donor
sites that splice into this exon shifts between 0 and 6 hours.

The jump at 6 hours partly reflects which donors are used:

- **CD_21** has a large effect at every timepoint: REF 92% vs ALT 15% inclusion
  at 0 hours, 86% vs 6% at 6 hours.
- **CD_48** shows no difference at 0 hours, from only 8 ALT reads, and a large
  one at 6 hours (85% vs 19%).
- **CD_36** has an inconsistent effect (−19 pp at 0 hours, +8 pp at 1 hour)
  and no reads at 6 hours.

## ASAH1

The tested part is a 115-base alternative first exon: ASAH1-264 starts with it,
and the other transcripts start at another first exon. isoLASER counts ALT (A)
reads as using it more often than REF (G) reads at 1 hour (+21 pp,
q = `r qv("ASAH1", "1hr")`). At 0 and 6 hours the difference is +7 and +8 pp, below threshold.
The 1-hour test uses two donors (CD_21 and CD_31); 0 and 6 hours use CD_21
only. The tested SNP (rs7508) is in the last exon, about 19 kb away in the
genome, and about half of the reads reach the plotted region.

## LMBRD1

The first exon ends at one of two donor sites, an alternative 5′ splice site,
and the 77-base part is the extra stretch of the longer first exon in
LMBRD1-225. isoLASER counts nearly all ALT (A) reads as including it and no REF
(G) reads: +93 pp at 6 hours (q = `r qv("LMBRD1", "6hr")`).

- **0 hours:** a similar difference, +74 pp, but from 35 reads in two donors
  and below threshold (nominal p = `r pv("LMBRD1", "0hr")`).
- **1 hour:** +85 pp, from only one qualifying donor.
- **The gene at 1 hour:** it is reported through a different part.

The tested SNP (rs9185) is in the last exon, about 120 kb away in the genome.
rs3752787, 113 bases from the part, is in phase with it (C on the A
haplotype). Few reads reach the plotted region (8 of 76 at 6 hours).

# All reported genes

Here, **reported** means q < 0.05 plus the `cis` / effect-size screen.

```{r patterns}
pat <- g[, .N, by=pattern][match(names(pattern_labels), pattern)][!is.na(pattern)]
knitr::kable(pat[, .(Pattern=unname(pattern_labels[pattern]), Genes=N)], align="lr")
```

For genes reported at one timepoint, the last three categories describe the
representative association at the other timepoints: nominal p < 0.05, p ≥ 0.05
where scored, or no usable score. They are not tests of an allele × time
interaction. Among comparisons of significant associations with another
timepoint, `r pct(cons$nominal_p_lt_0.05)` had nominal p < 0.05 there and
`r pct(cons$same_sign)` had the same effect direction.

## Full interactive gene table

All **`r nrow(g)` reported genes**. The variant, part, timepoint effects, best q
and donor count refer to the representative association; **Significant at**
describes the gene across all its associations. **With filter** marks genes also
reported in the run with the clustering filter.

```{r all}
interactive_table(cbind(g[, .(Gene=gene, Pattern=display_pattern, `Significant at`=sig_tps,
  `0 hr`=effect_reads(g, "0hr"), `1 hr`=effect_reads(g, "1hr"), `6 hr`=effect_reads(g, "6hr"),
  `Best q`=best_q(g), `Het donors`=max_het,
  `With filter`=fifelse(gene %in% both_genes, "yes", "no"))], annot(g),
  g[, .(Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part)]))
```

**0 / 1 / 6 hr**: allelic effect in percentage points, alternative minus
reference inclusion, with pooled informative coverage in brackets. The
annotations use the same rules as on the
[original page](isolaser_fdr.html#full-interactive-gene-table).

**Data:** `10.isolaser_permutation/` with `ADAPTIVE_RULE=panel10nc`: run by
`logs/family_rule_driver.sh panel10nc` (scripts 38 and 18–22, with the independent
score check 48 / 50), and compared with the run with the clustering filter by
`53.compare_family_rules.R`. This page's tables come from
`11.fdr_results/3.page_tables.R` with `ADAPTIVE_RULE=panel10nc`, which writes only
to `docs/assets/fdr_panel10nc/`.
